Settings.help: Where app ports listen. Keep 127.0.0.1: other devices go through the proxy.
Where the proxy (80/443) and DNS (53) listen. 0.0.0.0 follows the Mac's address, so a new IP (Wi-Fi vs Ethernet) never breaks them.
Where AdGuard Home's DNS (53) listens, when not LAN_BIND_IP. Set to this machine's address on Linux when systemd-resolved holds 127.0.0.53:53, which a 0.0.0.0 bind would collide with.

Docker's socket, for the apps that talk to Docker (the socket proxy and Beszel's agent). Empty: /var/run/docker.sock. With Docker run as you (SteamOS, homelab runtime install), your own: /run/user/<your id>/docker.sock.

How the homelab reads the containers, their events, and what they use, and runs commands in them (the database copies): auto (the engine's API over its socket, found as the docker CLI finds it, with the docker command whenever that fails) or off (the docker command only). Starting and updating apps is docker compose either way.

How containers reach this machine's own apps (Jellyfin, the phone companion, Ollama) as host.docker.internal. Empty: Docker's host-gateway. With Docker run as you, this machine's address (host-gateway is then Docker's own namespace).
Keep this machine from sleeping while it is plugged in, so the apps stay reachable (the screen still turns off). false lets it sleep as set.

On a laptop running on battery, pause the apps that work hardest in the background (downloads, the *arr apps, photo recognition) and start them again once it is plugged in; the watchdog checks every 15 minutes. false keeps them.
The phone companion (homelab serve, the serve job): Status and Backups on paired phones, on port 8099, home network and tailnet only. false: off.
The media drive. Apps that use it wait for it to be mounted.
Where Duplicati writes encrypted backups: your Proton Drive folder, e.g. /Users/you/Library/CloudStorage/ProtonDrive-you@proton.me-folder/homelab-backups
Where Kopia (optional, a second backup beside Duplicati) keeps its repository: best another drive than this machine's own, e.g. /Volumes/Backup/kopia.
Native Jellyfin's data folder (Jellyfin > Dashboard > Paths shows it).
Syncthing's shared folders (backed up only if you add it to a Duplicati job).

small: `up` starts only updates, backups, and alerts (x-homelab-small-baseline in compose.yaml), and you pick every other app; folders the desktop app makes start this way. Empty or full: every app without a profile, as in this repo.
Empty (the default): Home mode, every app at an https address on your tailnet through Tailscale, with no domain, AdGuard rewrites, Cloudflare, or tunnel.

The phone companion's proxy key, made by Set up the domain: the companion's proxy host sends it, so the companion knows a phone reached it over https and not over the Wi-Fi (docs/Security.md, N25). Left empty until then.

Give each app its https://<name>.<domain> address in Nginx Proxy Manager (and the tunnel, for public apps) as soon as it is installed, once Set up the domain has run. false: only when you run Set up the domain.
For the wildcard certificate (./homelab domain setup --ssl) and the tunnel's public hostnames. Token permissions: Zone.Zone:Read, Zone.DNS:Edit, and Account.Cloudflare Tunnel:Edit.
From Cloudflare Zero Trust > Networks > Tunnels > your tunnel > Docker.

The account the CLI uses, created on NPM's first start; Let's Encrypt also registers certificates with this email. Keep 2FA off for this account (2FA blocks the API) and make your personal admin with 2FA instead.
Optional: enrolls CrowdSec in app.crowdsec.net (console > Engines > Add).
AdGuard's login: homelab adguard setup makes it in the first-run wizard, or put in the one you made there. The CLI uses it to add the *.domain rewrite.
Alerts also show on this machine's screen (Notification Center on a Mac), even before the phone gets them. false: the phone only.
The night: alerts between these hours reach the phone without a sound, unless they are serious (the vault unreachable, backups failing for two days). 22-7 is 22:00 to 07:00; off sounds every alert.
Who helps you with the homelab: Setup's Email it to my helper writes to them with the diagnostics report.
The publishers' ntfy access token, and the same as a ?auth= parameter for publishers that only take a URL. ./homelab notify setup fills both in.
A read-only token for the desktop app's list of recent alerts (notify setup).
The phone's ntfy login (user "phone"), made by notify setup; copy it from Settings.

An external heartbeat, such as a healthchecks.io check's ping URL (period 15 minutes, grace 15 minutes). The watchdog pings it every run and pings /fail when something is down, so you hear about it even when this machine, its runtime, or ntfy is down.
When the background agent runs the nightly updates (4:00 by default). The name is from Watchtower, which ran them before.
The socket proxy holds Docker's socket, so it stays on this version until you choose a newer one: read the release notes, change the version, then ./homelab update docker-socket-proxy.
The Beszel agent holds Docker's socket too: the same, then ./homelab update beszel-agent.
Frigate stays on this version until you choose a newer one: read the release notes (a new version can change its settings file), then ./homelab update frigate.
Kopia stays on this version until you choose a newer one: read the release notes, then ./homelab update kopia.
Which homelab updates homelab upgrade gets: stable (tagged releases) or testing (every change on main, the default until the first release).
The largest folder or volume copied before an app's update, so a rollback can put it back (500MB, 10GB; 0 copies any size). Databases are always dumped.
The watchdog rolls back an app that stays unhealthy after its nightly update, and holds its updates. false: it only alerts.
The watchdog restarts an app that is unhealthy or not answering on two checks in a row (once in 6 hours at most). false: it only alerts.
The Ollama model that explains logs (Explain this log), e.g. llama3.2. Empty: the first Llama, Qwen, Gemma, Mistral, or Phi model Ollama has.
Apps whose updates are held after a rollback, or by hand. Written by homelab rollback and homelab updates hold|release.

Tidy Up sorts, tags, and shrinks the libraries on the media drive (MEDIA_ROOT): music, books, movies, tv, audiobooks. false turns its background work off (the inbox, Tdarr's finished work, and the nightly scrubber); the screen still works.
File what finishes downloading in Downloads, and in DOWNLOADS_ROOT, into the libraries. Other folders to watch instead: TIDY_INBOX_FOLDERS, separated by ;.
Every night at 03:00, put leftovers whose film, song, or book is gone (posters, .nfo and subtitle files, empty folders) in the Trash.
The audio and subtitle languages films and episodes keep (ISO 639-2, e.g. eng, jpn); the rest are removed when Tdarr shrinks them.
What Tdarr shrinks video to: hevc (plays everywhere) or av1 (smaller, newer players).
New lossless music (FLAC, WAV) is stored as 256k AAC, about a fifth of the size. false keeps it lossless.
Lyrics: embed (inside each song file) or lrc (a .lrc file beside each song).
Where beets runs for music: local (this computer, fastest) or container (the beets image). Empty: local when Python can make its own environment here.
A Plex server to tell about each new or changed file (Plex › Settings › Network shows its address), its token, and how its folders map to this computer's, e.g. /Volumes/Media=/data.
Audiobookshelf's API key (Settings › Users › your user › API token): Tidy Up tells it about new files.
Tidy Up's key to Tdarr, generated: Tdarr takes it as its own when it starts (seededApiKey), since Tdarr 3 takes no sign-up.
Tdarr's sign-in, for an older Tdarr: made by Tidy Up (user homelab) when Tdarr had no account yet; if you made one in Tdarr first, put its user name and password here.

Settings.help: Where Navidrome sees the music folder in its container. Empty: the same path as on this machine, so playlists with full paths keep working (Mac and Linux). Windows sets /music, since a C:\ path cannot be one there.

A Navidrome administrator's login, best one of its own (Navidrome › Users › Create, e.g. homelab, with Is Admin on). With it, Settings › People makes each person's Navidrome account and gives them a new password when they need one.

A Jellyfin API key (Dashboard › API Keys › +, named Homelab). With it, Settings › People makes each person's Jellyfin account (for Infuse and the TV apps too) and gives them a new password when they need one.
Turn on only while creating accounts, then back off (./homelab doctor warns).

The backup jobs' encryption passphrases (homelab duplicati setup uses them). Keep DUPLICATI_SECRETS_PASSPHRASE outside this machine too, in Vaultwarden and on the recovery kit: it opens the Secrets backup, which holds this file.
Kopia's repository password: it opens every Kopia backup, so keep it outside this machine too, with DUPLICATI_SECRETS_PASSPHRASE. The other is its web page's.
Its PostgreSQL major version; change it only with homelab db upgrade.
A token made in Paperless-ngx (your account › My Profile › API Auth Token); Paperless-AI installs once it is set.
The password Frigate and Home Assistant use on Frigate's event broker.
Nextcloud's administrator (made on its first start) and its database.
Its PostgreSQL major version; change it only with homelab db upgrade.
Nextcloud's major version: the nightly updates bring its fixes; a new major is set here (one at a time) after a backup, then ./homelab update nextcloud.
Pocket ID encrypts its keys with this; losing it means re-registering passkeys.
The key homelab sso setup uses on Pocket ID's API to connect the apps.
Pocket ID's name, which the apps' containers reach through the proxy here. Written by homelab sso setup.
PsiTransfer: the admin page's password, and the one needed to upload (leave the upload one set so only the household can send files).
Homebox: turn off once everyone has an account.
Homebox signs the API keys it gives with this (32 characters or more); changing it ends every one of them.
Its PostgreSQL major version; change it only with homelab db upgrade.
Optional: artwork and game details for RomM (services/media/RomM.md).
Its PostgreSQL major version; change it only with homelab db upgrade.
Changing either of these later signs everyone out of Ghostfolio for good.

Your Ghostfolio security token (the one you sign in with): Finances reads your investments with it, on Net worth's Investments card (Read now, then once a day) and in Update balances. Press Read now there to check it works.
Its PostgreSQL major version; change it only with homelab db upgrade.
Changing it later signs everyone out of Docmost.
Its PostgreSQL major version; change it only with homelab db upgrade.
Changing it later signs everyone out of Tandoor.

Empty runs MoneyMatter's Intel images under Rosetta. To run the frontend and backend natively, build them from source (services/finance/MoneyMatter.md) and set homelab/moneymatter-frontend:v0.30.2, homelab/moneymatter-backend:v0.30.2, and linux/arm64.
Its PostgreSQL major version; change it only with homelab db upgrade.
Firefly III encrypts with FIREFLY_APP_KEY (32 characters): keep it with the backup.
A personal access token from Firefly III (Profile › OAuth), for its data importer; Finances › Update balances reads the asset accounts' balances with it too, on a click.
Wallos's API key (Profile › API Key): Finances › Recurring reads its subscriptions with it, on a click.
Beszel's first account, made on its first start.
The hub's public key, from Beszel's Add System; the agent starts once it is set.
Optional qBittorrent VPN (ProtonVPN account > Downloads > WireGuard).
Tailscale: a reusable auth key from login.tailscale.com > Settings > Keys, and the home network it makes reachable (set from this machine's network; approve the route in the admin).
Extra flags for tailscale up, as --login-server=https://headscale.example.com for a tailnet on your own Headscale server. Empty: Tailscale's own.
Home mode (HOMELAB_DOMAIN empty): this machine's tailnet name, written by homelab tailnet setup. Every app is at https://<TAILSCALE_HOST>:<its port>.

Home mode: false keeps the admin apps (the proxy, AdGuard, Duplicati, Dozzle, and the like) off the tailnet, so only this machine opens them; the household apps stay on it. true (the default) serves every app.

The address each app is opened at, for the apps that need to know it (sign-in, links in emails). Empty: https://<subdomain>.<domain>. In Home mode homelab tailnet setup writes the tailnet address. MoneyMatter only signs in at exactly its address.
Off once the household has its accounts (the first one is the administrator).
